title: The Evening Brief: Fear Gauge Sits at 29 as Bitcoin Holds Near $75,100
dek: No new desk stories published today. The picture comes entirely from the desk's own boards: a market in Fear, bitcoin alone holding its 200-day average, and a mixed week of exchange flows.
author: GoCheckMyCrypto
key_fact: With no fresh reporting today, the desk's boards show a market still in Fear (29) even as bitcoin trades up 0.08% over 24 hours near $75,103, while ETF outflows and falling stablecoin supply point to caution beneath the calm surface.

body: The desk published no new stories today, so this edition reports what its own boards show rather than new developments. The headline fact is simple: bitcoin sits at $75,103, up 0.08% over 24 hours, even as the broader Fear and Greed Index reads 29, squarely in Fear territory and near the low end of its 30-day range of 25 to 69.

With no wire to weave together, the picture is the tape itself. Bitcoin is down 4.54% over seven days and down 9.48% over thirty days, a decline that has not broken its 200-day simple moving average or its golden cross, both of which the desk's boards still show intact. Ether tells a different story: down 0.93% over 24 hours, down 6.58% over seven days and down 14.54% over thirty days, and unlike bitcoin, Ether remains below its 200-day simple moving average even though it too still shows a golden cross. Solana, XRP, Cardano and Dogecoin all show similar or steeper declines over the week and month, with RSI readings in the mid-to-high 20s across SOL, XRP, DOGE and ADA, consistent with a broadly oversold tape rather than an isolated move in any one asset.

The reporting does not say what is driving the selloff, since no stories were published today to supply a cause. What the boards do show is a market where price has fallen further and faster than sentiment has recovered: the Fear and Greed Index at 29 sits well below the top of its own 30-day range, and RSI readings below 40 across every tracked asset point to a market that has been sold without yet showing technical exhaustion.

The desk's Whale Watch board shows $182,675,346 in bitcoin moving off exchanges over the past 72 hours, a figure the board's own convention reads as accumulation or self-custody rather than selling pressure. That reading sits alongside a mixed picture over recent weeks: the week ending Nov 02 saw $5,510 million in net flows off exchanges, and the week ending Nov 09 saw $1,569 million off exchanges, following a week ending Oct 26 in which $1,549 million moved onto exchanges. On the stablecoin side, the board shows $82,969,839 in net stablecoin buying power moving onto exchanges over the same 72-hour window, alongside $196,860,551 in USDT moving off Poloniex and $179,793,890 in USDT moving onto Poloniex, a pattern the board does not explain further. Spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of $411.9M on the day, November 6, and net outflows of $1,281.7M over the week through November 6, a figure that sits in tension with the bitcoin accumulation signal from the Whale Watch board. Total stablecoin supply is down 4.26% over 30 days to $292,973,703,177, consistent with capital leaving the stablecoin complex rather than flowing into it. Leverage data from OKX shows funding rates mild and positive across BTC, SOL, XRP and DOGE, with ETH funding essentially flat, and long-short ratios skewed toward longs across the board, while liquidations over the trailing windows lean toward shorts being liquidated more than longs in BTC and ETH specifically.

With no stories published today, there is nothing new to check against the regulatory calendar beyond what the desk has already covered. The live threads the desk has reported stay open: the CLARITY Act in the United States, the Markets in Crypto-Assets framework and MiCA rules in the European Union, and the measures the desk has tracked in Japan, Russia and the United States tied to sanctions enforcement and custody rulemaking. None of these carry a new checkpoint date beyond what the desk has already stated in its prior reporting, and no new developments on any of them arrived today. The coming days will test whether the ETF outflow pattern persists beyond the week through November 6, whether bitcoin's hold above its 200-day average continues as the Fear and Greed Index stays depressed, and whether the net flows off exchanges seen over the past two weeks extend into a third.
